Add status from spell data to a panel you already have

Source: R/add_spell_status.R
add_spell_status.Rd

spells_to_panel() builds a panel from spells. Often the panel already exists, e.g. a population with one row per person and year, or events with a date, and the spell data should only add a status to it: was the person enrolled at the end of the year, on leave on the day of the diagnosis? add_spell_status() looks up the spell covering each row's point in time and adds its status as new column(s).

Usage

add_spell_status(
  data,
  spells,
  id,
  at,
  start,
  end,
  status,
  by = c("year", "quarter", "month"),
  when = c("both", "primo", "ultimo"),
  status_is = c("state", "outcome"),
  ongoing = "ongoing",
  primo = c("previous_ultimo", "first_day"),
  overlap = c("latest_start", "error"),
  name = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, e.g. a panel with one row per unit and period. Its rows and columns are kept as they are.

spells

A data frame with one row per spell.

id

Column(s) identifying the unit (tidy-select, in data), e.g. cpr. spells must have columns of the same names; rename first if not.

at

Column(s) in data with the point in time: a Date column, or a year column, or a year and a quarter/month column. See Details.

start, end, status

Columns in spells, as in spells_to_panel().

by

Period of at when it is not a date: "year", "quarter" or "month". Ignored for a Date at.

when

For periods: "both" (default) adds a primo and an ultimo column, "primo" or "ultimo" adds one. Ignored for a Date at.

status_is, ongoing, primo

As in spells_to_panel().

overlap

"latest_start" (default) or "error". Only state mode checks overlaps; in outcome mode the most recently ended spell decides.

name

Name of the new column. Defaults to the name of status, with _primo and _ultimo appended for periods. With when = "both", name is the prefix for the two columns.

Value

data with the new column(s) added at the end, same class.

Details

It exists because an interval join, e.g. dplyr::left_join() with join_by(between()), goes wrong exactly where register data is messy: overlapping spells duplicate panel rows silently, an ongoing spell with a missing end matches nothing, and an outcome (passed, dropped out) cannot be carried forward. Here the rows of data are never added, dropped or reordered, and the rules are those of spells_to_panel(): on a yearly panel, add_spell_status(panel, spells, cpr, year, ...) gives the same primo and ultimo status as spells_to_panel() joined on cpr and year.

The point in time comes from at:

  • A Date column: the status on that day, one new column.

  • A year column (with by = "year"), or a year and a quarter or month column (with by = "quarter" or "month"): the status at primo and/or ultimo of the period, chosen with when. Primo follows primo, as in spells_to_panel() and age().

status_is, ongoing and the treatment of overlapping spells are as in spells_to_panel(): the latest start wins, with a message counting the points where this happened. Use overlap = "error" to stop instead, e.g. in a pipeline that must fail hard. Rows whose unit has no spells, or whose point is missing, get NA. Spells with a missing start, or an end before the start, are dropped with a message.

See also

spells_to_panel() to build the panel from the spells, expectr::expect_no_overlap() to check the spells first.

Examples

education <- data.frame(
  cpr    = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start  = as.Date(c("2018-08-15", "2021-08-15", "2019-08-15")),
  end    = as.Date(c("2021-06-20", NA,           "2020-03-01")),
  status = c("passed", "in progress", "dropped out")
)
population <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "a", "b", "c"),
                         year = c(2020, 2021, 2020, 2020))

# primo and ultimo status for each person and year
add_spell_status(population, education, cpr, year, start, end, status,
                 status_is = "outcome", ongoing = "in progress")
#>   cpr year status_primo status_ultimo
#> 1   a 2020  in progress   in progress
#> 2   a 2021  in progress   in progress
#> 3   b 2020  in progress   dropped out
#> 4   c 2020         <NA>          <NA>

# status on the day of an event
events <- data.frame(cpr = c("a", "b"),
                     date = as.Date(c("2019-05-01", "2021-01-01")))
add_spell_status(events, education, cpr, date, start, end, status,
                 status_is = "outcome", ongoing = "in progress",
                 name = "education")
#>   cpr       date   education
#> 1   a 2019-05-01 in progress
#> 2   b 2021-01-01 dropped out
